h: Hydrangeas, china and boats on the Fal
p: Trelissick's garden is known for its hydrangeas, which thrive in the mild, damp Cornish air and put on a big show of blues, pinks and whites through late summer. Spring brings camellias, magnolias and rhododendrons, so whatever time of year you visit, there is usually something flowering.

Inside the house, look out for the collection of Copeland china, linked to the family who owned the estate in the 20th century. It is a lovely detail for anyone who enjoys pottery and fine table settings.

One of the best things about Trelissick is how it connects to the river. In the warmer months, passenger boats along the Fal call at the estate's pontoon, so you can arrive by water from Truro or Falmouth and turn the day into a proper adventure. Check the river boat timetables for current services.
Allow at least half a day, especially if you want to explore the woodland walks down to the shore. Bring a picnic, find a bench above the water and watch the boats drift by on Carrick Roads.

Truro is a short drive back, with its striking cathedral, Georgian Lemon Street and lively shops and cafés. Falmouth is also close, with the National Maritime Museum Cornwall and its busy harbour. Cross on the King Harry Ferry and you can head down the Roseland peninsula to St Mawes, with its Tudor castle and pretty waterfront.
Wear decent shoes, as the paths down to the water can be steep in places.
